audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-006: Is BlobSidecarsByRoot deprecated protocol fully disabled after FULU_FORK_EPOCH + MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOB_SIDECARS_REQUESTS?
audit_items.code_excerpt_summary: The handle_blobs_by_root_request function handles BlobSidecarsByRoot requests. It has a TODO comment at line 1395 indicating MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOB_SIDECARS_REQUESTS is not yet implemented. The function currently serves blobs without epoch-based deprecation checks.

phase1_structural_analysis.findings: The BlobSidecarsByRoot handler lacks epoch-based deprecation logic. The TODO at line 1395 confirms this is incomplete.

phase2_semantic_analysis.findings: Missing implementation of protocol deprecation after FULU_FORK_EPOCH + MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOB_SIDECARS_REQUESTS. The current code serves all requested blobs without verifying the epoch-based deprecation window.
phase2_semantic_analysis.attack_vectors: Post-deprecation, an attacker could continue requesting blobs via this protocol, wasting server resources on a deprecated endpoint.

phase3_classification.reasoning: The TODO comment explicitly acknowledges this implementation gap. The deprecated protocol should reject requests after the transition period ends.
phase3_classification.recommended_action: Implement epoch-based deprecation check: reject requests when current_epoch >= FULU_FORK_EPOCH + MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOB_SIDECARS_REQUESTS

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Does beacon-node correctly identify pre-Fulu vs post-Fulu blobs by root during transition period?
audit_items.code_excerpt_summary: The function calls controller.blob_sidecars_by_ids() without any epoch filtering. There is no logic to distinguish pre-Fulu vs post-Fulu blobs during the transition period.

phase1_structural_analysis.findings: No epoch-based filtering in blob retrieval. The blob_sidecars_by_ids function is called directly without transition period checks.

phase2_semantic_analysis.findings: During the transition period, the protocol should only serve pre-Fulu blobs. The current implementation lacks this epoch-based filtering.
phase2_semantic_analysis.attack_vectors: Could serve post-Fulu data through deprecated protocol, causing inconsistent behavior.

phase3_classification.reasoning: Linked to CHK-0001. The lack of epoch-based checks means the protocol cannot properly identify and filter pre-Fulu vs post-Fulu blobs.
phase3_classification.recommended_action: Add epoch validation before serving blobs to ensure only pre-Fulu blobs are served during transition.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-001/tb-002: Is max_blobs_per_block from get_blob_parameters(epoch) consistent across all client implementations?
audit_items.code_excerpt_summary: This check requires cross-client comparison of get_blob_parameters() implementations across Lighthouse, Prysm, Teku, Lodestar, Nimbus, and Grandine.

phase1_structural_analysis.findings: In Grandine, max_blobs_per_block is configured via types/src/config.rs. The value is stored as a config parameter rather than computed dynamically.

phase2_semantic_analysis.findings: Grandine uses static configuration for max_blobs_per_block. Cross-client consistency requires comparing all implementations.
phase2_semantic_analysis.attack_vectors: Cross-client parameter mismatch at fork boundaries could cause consensus splits.

phase3_classification.reasoning: This check requires multi-client testing environment and comparison across 6+ client implementations. Single-client code audit cannot verify cross-client consistency.
phase3_classification.recommended_action: Requires cross-client integration testing in a multi-client devnet environment.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Does beacon-node correctly enforce max_blobs_per_block limit during block/sidecar gossip validation?
audit_items.code_excerpt_summary: The validate_data_column_sidecar_with_state function calls verify_data_column_sidecar() which checks if kzg_commitments.is_empty(). The max_blobs_per_block enforcement is implicit through container size limits.

phase1_structural_analysis.findings: verify_data_column_sidecar in eip_7594/src/lib.rs:147-172 validates structural properties but doesn't explicitly check max_blobs_per_block. The ContiguousList type provides implicit bounds.

phase2_semantic_analysis.findings: The max_blobs_per_block is enforced via SSZ type bounds (MaxBlobCommitmentsPerBlock). This occurs during deserialization before validation.
phase2_semantic_analysis.attack_vectors: If deserialization doesn't properly enforce bounds, oversized blobs could reach validation logic.

phase3_classification.reasoning: The Rust type system with ContiguousList<..., P::MaxBlobCommitmentsPerBlock> enforces the limit at deserialization time. This is defense-in-depth through type safety.
phase3_classification.recommended_action: Verify SSZ deserialization correctly rejects oversized blob commitments lists.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-010/tb-011: Is proposer lookahead (EIP-7917) deterministic and consistent across all client implementations?
audit_items.code_excerpt_summary: EIP-7917 proposer lookahead consistency requires cross-client verification.

phase1_structural_analysis.findings: Grandine uses accessors::get_beacon_proposer_index() for proposer computation. Implementation in helper_functions/src/accessors.rs.

phase2_semantic_analysis.findings: Proposer index computation relies on shuffling algorithm and RANDAO. Cross-client consistency requires all clients implement identical shuffling.
phase2_semantic_analysis.attack_vectors: Shuffling divergence causes different proposer assignments, enabling consensus splits.

phase3_classification.reasoning: Cross-client consistency verification requires multi-client testing infrastructure.
phase3_classification.recommended_action: Verify through consensus-spec-tests and multi-client devnets.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Does gossip validation correctly reject sidecars with incorrect proposer_index?
audit_items.code_excerpt_summary: Lines 2193-2207 validate proposer_index: computed = accessors::get_beacon_proposer_index(); ensure!(block_header.proposer_index == computed). This REJECTS on mismatch.

phase1_structural_analysis.findings: The proposer_index check at lines 2199-2207 computes expected proposer and rejects on mismatch with Error::DataColumnSidecarProposerIndexMismatch.

phase2_semantic_analysis.findings: Proposer validation is correctly implemented - computes expected proposer from state and rejects if sidecar.proposer_index doesn't match. This check is skipped for back_sync origin.
phase2_semantic_analysis.attack_vectors: Back sync bypass could allow incorrect proposer_index during historical sync, but this is expected behavior for trusted sync sources.

phase3_classification.reasoning: The implementation correctly rejects sidecars with incorrect proposer_index through the ensure! macro which returns Error on mismatch.
phase3_classification.recommended_action: None required. Implementation is correct.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Does the proposer lookahead window correctly handle fork transitions at FULU_FORK_EPOCH?
audit_items.code_excerpt_summary: The proposer computation uses the provided state which should reflect the correct fork. The get_beacon_proposer_index function handles fork-specific logic.

phase1_structural_analysis.findings: Fork handling is implicit through the BeaconState type which carries fork information. The chain_config is passed to ensure correct domain computation.

phase2_semantic_analysis.findings: The proposer index computation at fork transitions depends on correct state being provided. The state_fn() callback retrieves appropriate state for the slot.
phase2_semantic_analysis.attack_vectors: If incorrect state (pre-fork vs post-fork) is used at FULU_FORK_EPOCH boundary, proposer computation could diverge.

phase3_classification.reasoning: The implementation retrieves state appropriate for the block's slot. Fork transitions are handled by the state type system.
phase3_classification.recommended_action: Verify through fork transition tests at FULU_FORK_EPOCH boundaries.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-001: Is KZG commitment verification cryptographically sound against forged data column sidecars?
audit_items.code_excerpt_summary:
verify_kzg_proofs calls verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch::

() from kzg_utils crate. This uses external KZG library implementations (arkworks, blst, constantine, etc.).

phase1_structural_analysis.findings: KZG verification delegates to kzg_utils::eip_7594::verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch which calls library-specific implementations. Multiple backends supported.

phase2_semantic_analysis.findings: Cryptographic soundness depends on the underlying KZG libraries (kzg crate). The Grandine code correctly orchestrates the verification calls.
phase2_semantic_analysis.attack_vectors: Implementation bugs in the underlying KZG library could allow forged proofs. This requires auditing the dependency.

phase3_classification.reasoning: The wrapper code correctly delegates to battle-tested KZG libraries. Cryptographic soundness depends on library correctness which is outside this codebase.
phase3_classification.recommended_action: Ensure KZG library dependencies are audited and up-to-date.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Is inclusion proof verification correctly integrated with KZG commitment verification?
audit_items.code_excerpt_summary: Lines 2176-2191 verify both inclusion proof and KZG proofs sequentially. Both must pass for sidecar acceptance. verify_sidecar_inclusion_proof is called first, then verify_kzg_proofs.

phase1_structural_analysis.findings: Both verifications are required: line 2178-2183 calls verify_sidecar_inclusion_proof, lines 2185-2190 call verify_kzg_proofs. Both use ensure! to reject on failure.

phase2_semantic_analysis.findings: Correct integration: inclusion proof verified before KZG proofs. Both must pass. The origin.is_from_el() check bypasses these for execution layer sourced data (trusted).
phase2_semantic_analysis.attack_vectors: EL-sourced data bypasses cryptographic verification. This is intentional for trusted local execution layer data.

phase3_classification.reasoning: Both KZG and inclusion proof verifications are required for gossip-sourced sidecars. The EL bypass is appropriate for trusted local data.
phase3_classification.recommended_action: None required.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Does KZG proof batch verification maintain soundness properties of individual verification?
audit_items.code_excerpt_summary: verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch delegates to verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch_raw from the kzg crate. The batch verification implementation is in the external library.

phase1_structural_analysis.findings: The function transforms input types and delegates to the appropriate backend (arkworks, blst, constantine, mcl, zkcrypto). Soundness depends on library implementation.

phase2_semantic_analysis.findings: Batch verification soundness is a property of the underlying cryptographic library. The wrapper code correctly passes all necessary parameters.
phase2_semantic_analysis.attack_vectors: Flaws in batch aggregation could allow invalid proofs to pass. This is a library-level concern.

phase3_classification.reasoning: Batch verification soundness is a cryptographic library property. The Grandine code correctly uses the library API.
phase3_classification.recommended_action: Defer to KZG library security audits (kzg crate).

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-001: Are structural validation checks performed BEFORE expensive KZG/inclusion proof verification in the gossip validation pipeline?
audit_items.code_excerpt_summary: Validation order: 1) verify_data_column_sidecar (structural, line 2050-2056), 2) subnet check (2058-2072), 3) slot checks (2074-2083), 4) duplicate check (2085-2094), 5) state retrieval, 6) signature verification (2106-2116), 7) parent checks, 8) KZG verification (2176-2190).

phase1_structural_analysis.findings: Structural checks (verify_data_column_sidecar) are performed first at line 2050-2056. KZG verification is last at lines 2185-2190. Correct ordering.

phase2_semantic_analysis.findings: The validation pipeline correctly orders cheap checks before expensive ones. However, signature verification (line 2106-2116) occurs before KZG verification, which is appropriate as signatures are cheaper than KZG.
phase2_semantic_analysis.attack_vectors: Current ordering is correct. Attackers cannot trigger expensive KZG verification without passing structural checks first.

phase3_classification.reasoning: The validation order is: structural -> slot/finalized checks -> signature -> parent checks -> KZG. This correctly prioritizes cheap checks.
phase3_classification.recommended_action: None required. Validation ordering is correct.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Does proposer signature verification act as effective cost gate before KZG verification?
audit_items.code_excerpt_summary: Signature verification at lines 2106-2116 uses SingleVerifier.verify_singular(). This occurs BEFORE KZG verification (lines 2185-2190), acting as a cost gate.

phase1_structural_analysis.findings: Signature verification is at line 2106-2116. KZG verification is at 2185-2190. Signature check acts as cost gate - invalid signatures rejected before expensive KZG.

phase2_semantic_analysis.findings: BLS signature verification (~1ms) is much cheaper than KZG batch verification. This ordering prevents attackers from triggering expensive KZG with forged sidecars.
phase2_semantic_analysis.attack_vectors: Without signature check as gate, attackers could trigger KZG verification with any forged sidecar. Current ordering prevents this.

phase3_classification.reasoning: Signature verification correctly precedes KZG verification, acting as an effective cost gate.
phase3_classification.recommended_action: None required.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Are all structural validation checks O(1) complexity relative to sidecar size?
audit_items.code_excerpt_summary: verify_data_column_sidecar performs: 1) index bounds check (O(1)), 2) empty check (O(1)), 3) length equality checks (O(1) - comparing lengths not iterating).

phase1_structural_analysis.findings: All checks in verify_data_column_sidecar are O(1): index comparison, is_empty(), .len() comparisons. No iteration over data.

phase2_semantic_analysis.findings: Structural checks correctly use O(1) operations. Length comparisons use .len() which is O(1) for Rust Vec/ContiguousList types.
phase2_semantic_analysis.attack_vectors: O(1) checks prevent amplification attacks. Attackers cannot cause linear-time processing with structural validation.

phase3_classification.reasoning: All structural checks are O(1). The implementation correctly avoids iterating over sidecar data during validation.
phase3_classification.recommended_action: None required.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-003: Does DataColumnSidecarsByRange serve complete block responses (all columns or none) for columns in storage?
audit_items.code_excerpt_summary: The handler calls controller.data_column_sidecars_by_range() and sends all returned sidecars. Response completeness depends on the storage layer implementation.

phase1_structural_analysis.findings: Handler retrieves sidecars via data_column_sidecars_by_range() at line 1340, sorts them by (slot, column_index), and sends all. No explicit all-or-none logic.

phase2_semantic_analysis.findings: The atomicity property depends on fork_choice_control/src/queries.rs:data_column_sidecars_by_range() implementation. Need to verify storage layer atomicity.
phase2_semantic_analysis.attack_vectors: If partial columns are returned for a block, syncing nodes could incorrectly conclude data unavailability.

phase3_classification.reasoning: The handler sends whatever storage returns. Atomicity guarantee requires verifying the storage layer implementation.
phase3_classification.recommended_action: Verify data_column_sidecars_by_range in fork_choice_control provides atomic per-block responses.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Does the req-resp client correctly interpret partial block responses as unavailability?
audit_items.code_excerpt_summary: Client-side handling of DataColumnsByRange responses in block_sync_service.rs. Responses are processed via P2pToSync messages.

phase1_structural_analysis.findings: Response handling at p2p/src/network.rs:1691-1725 sends received sidecars to sync service. The sync manager tracks received sidecars.

phase2_semantic_analysis.findings: The client-side logic for handling partial responses needs verification in sync_manager. Retry logic should query other peers if partial data received.
phase2_semantic_analysis.attack_vectors: If partial responses are accepted as complete, nodes could incorrectly mark data as unavailable.

phase3_classification.reasoning: Response handling logic in sync_manager needs verification for partial response handling.
phase3_classification.recommended_action: Verify sync_manager retry logic for partial DataColumnsByRange responses.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Is there atomicity between storage check and response generation in DataColumnSidecarsByRange?
audit_items.code_excerpt_summary: The data_column_sidecars_by_range function retrieves sidecars from storage. Atomicity depends on database transaction handling.

phase1_structural_analysis.findings: Need to examine queries.rs:data_column_sidecars_by_range implementation for transaction boundaries.

phase2_semantic_analysis.findings: TOCTOU vulnerabilities could occur if columns are pruned between check and fetch. Database snapshot isolation needed.
phase2_semantic_analysis.attack_vectors: Race condition during pruning could cause partial block responses.

phase3_classification.reasoning: Storage layer atomicity requires examining database transaction implementation.
phase3_classification.recommended_action: Verify database operations use consistent snapshots/transactions.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-004: Does DataColumnSidecarsByRoot respond with at least one sidecar when matching data is available?
audit_items.code_excerpt_summary: Handler calls controller.data_column_sidecars_by_ids() at line 1528-1529 and returns all matching sidecars. No silent filtering observed.

phase1_structural_analysis.findings: The handler iterates through storage results and sends each matching sidecar. No filtering logic that would drop valid sidecars.

phase2_semantic_analysis.findings: Response completeness depends on data_column_sidecars_by_ids implementation. The handler doesn't add any filtering.
phase2_semantic_analysis.attack_vectors: If storage query fails silently, empty responses could be returned for available data.

phase3_classification.reasoning: The handler correctly returns all matching sidecars from storage. No silent dropping logic observed.
phase3_classification.recommended_action: Verify storage layer data_column_sidecars_by_ids returns all available matching sidecars.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Does the req-resp client correctly handle empty responses from DataColumnSidecarsByRoot?
audit_items.code_excerpt_summary: DataColumnsByRoot response handling sends received sidecars to sync service and logs stream termination.

phase1_structural_analysis.findings: Response handling at lines 1716-1728 sends sidecars via P2pToSync::RequestedDataColumnSidecar. Empty responses just terminate the stream.

phase2_semantic_analysis.findings: Empty responses are handled by stream termination without error. Retry logic depends on sync_manager implementation.
phase2_semantic_analysis.attack_vectors: Malicious peers returning empty responses for available data could prevent sync if no retry with other peers.

phase3_classification.reasoning: Stream termination handling is correct but retry logic with other peers needs verification.
phase3_classification.recommended_action: Verify sync_manager retries with other peers when DataColumnsByRoot returns empty.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Is there any filtering or rate-limiting logic in DataColumnSidecarsByRoot that could silently drop valid sidecars?
audit_items.code_excerpt_summary: The handler uses .take(max_request_data_column_sidecars) at line 1526 to limit response size. This could truncate responses.

phase1_structural_analysis.findings: Line 1523-1526 uses .take() to limit response to max_request_data_column_sidecars. This is DoS prevention but could truncate valid data.

phase2_semantic_analysis.findings: The .take() call limits response size for DoS prevention. If request exceeds limit, some valid sidecars are not returned. No error signaling for truncation.
phase2_semantic_analysis.attack_vectors: Large requests could be silently truncated without client knowing some data was dropped.

phase3_classification.reasoning: Response truncation via .take() doesn't signal to client that more data was available. Client might incorrectly conclude data is unavailable.
phase3_classification.recommended_action: Consider signaling truncation or ensure clients never request more than max_request_data_column_sidecars.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-004: Does DataColumnSidecarsByRoot refuse to serve sidecars for blocks that fail beacon-chain state transition?
audit_items.code_excerpt_summary: The handler calls controller.data_column_sidecars_by_ids() without explicit block validity check. Validity depends on storage layer semantics.

phase1_structural_analysis.findings: No explicit check for block state transition validity in the handler. The storage layer determines what sidecars are stored.

phase2_semantic_analysis.findings: The storage layer (fork_choice_control) should only store sidecars for validated blocks. Need to verify invalid block sidecars are not stored.
phase2_semantic_analysis.attack_vectors: If sidecars for invalid blocks are stored and served, this could act as a validity oracle.

phase3_classification.reasoning: Block validity filtering depends on storage layer implementation. Need to verify sidecars are only stored for validated blocks.
phase3_classification.recommended_action: Verify storage layer only persists sidecars for blocks that passed state transition.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Is block state transition validity correctly tracked and accessible to the DataColumnSidecarsByRoot handler?
audit_items.code_excerpt_summary: Block validity is tracked in fork_choice_store. The rejected_block_roots set tracks invalid blocks.

phase1_structural_analysis.findings: fork_choice_store tracks rejected_block_roots (line 2122-2129 in validation). Storage should not contain sidecars for rejected blocks.

phase2_semantic_analysis.findings: Invalid blocks are tracked in rejected_block_roots. The data_column_sidecars_by_ids query should respect this.
phase2_semantic_analysis.attack_vectors: If sidecars for rejected blocks remain accessible, validity oracle attack is possible.

phase3_classification.reasoning: Need to verify data_column_sidecars_by_ids filters out sidecars for rejected blocks.
phase3_classification.recommended_action: Verify storage query excludes sidecars associated with rejected_block_roots.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Are there any bypass paths that could serve data columns for invalid blocks?
audit_items.code_excerpt_summary: The handler has no special debug/admin paths. All requests go through controller.data_column_sidecars_by_ids().

phase1_structural_analysis.findings: No bypass paths in the P2P handler. The TODO at line 1514 notes MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS_REQUESTS is incomplete.

phase2_semantic_analysis.findings: No admin/debug paths observed in the handler. Block validity filtering should happen in storage layer.
phase2_semantic_analysis.attack_vectors: No obvious bypass paths in P2P layer. Validity check is storage layer responsibility.

phase3_classification.reasoning: No bypass paths in P2P handler layer. Validity filtering is correctly delegated to storage.
phase3_classification.recommended_action: None in P2P layer. Verify storage layer implementation.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-001: Does the gossip validation pipeline IGNORE (not REJECT) sidecars whose parent block has not yet been seen?
audit_items.code_excerpt_summary: Lines 2131-2137: When parent_info() returns None, the function returns DataColumnSidecarAction::DelayUntilParent(sidecar). This is IGNORE behavior, not REJECT.

phase1_structural_analysis.findings: Line 2133-2136 returns DataColumnSidecarAction::DelayUntilParent when parent is not found. This queues the sidecar for later processing (IGNORE).

phase2_semantic_analysis.findings: Correctly returns DelayUntilParent (IGNORE) when parent not seen. The sidecar is queued, not rejected. Peer is not penalized.
phase2_semantic_analysis.attack_vectors: Correct IGNORE behavior prevents penalizing peers during legitimate out-of-order arrival scenarios.

phase3_classification.reasoning: The implementation correctly uses DelayUntilParent (IGNORE) for unseen parent, not REJECT.
phase3_classification.recommended_action: None required. Implementation is correct.

audit_items.title: Critical Boundary Check: Is the IGNORE queue for unseen-parent sidecars bounded to prevent memory exhaustion?
audit_items.code_excerpt_summary: The DelayUntilParent sidecars are queued. Need to verify queue bounds in the processing layer.

phase1_structural_analysis.findings: The validate function returns DelayUntilParent action. Queue management is in the caller (fork_choice_control or p2p layer).

phase2_semantic_analysis.findings: Queue bounds need verification in the processing layer that handles DelayUntilParent actions. Unbounded queue enables memory exhaustion.
phase2_semantic_analysis.attack_vectors: Attacker floods sidecars with unique unseen parent roots, each requiring queue entry. Unbounded queue -> OOM.

phase3_classification.reasoning: Queue bounds need verification in fork_choice_control task processing layer.
phase3_classification.recommended_action: Verify pending sidecar queue has bounded size and eviction policy.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Does the beacon-node correctly trigger re-validation of queued sidecars when the parent block arrives?
audit_items.code_excerpt_summary: Re-validation trigger logic should be in the mutator when processing new blocks. Pending sidecars should be re-checked.

phase1_structural_analysis.findings: Need to examine fork_choice_control/src/mutator.rs for pending sidecar re-validation on block arrival.

phase2_semantic_analysis.findings: When parent block arrives, queued sidecars with matching parent_root should be re-validated.
phase2_semantic_analysis.attack_vectors: If re-validation doesn't trigger, valid sidecars remain stuck in queue indefinitely.

phase3_classification.reasoning: Re-validation trigger logic needs verification in mutator.
phase3_classification.recommended_action: Verify mutator triggers re-validation of pending sidecars when their parent block arrives.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Are sidecars in the IGNORE queue protected from causing processing amplification attacks?
audit_items.code_excerpt_summary: DelayUntilParent is returned before expensive validation (KZG). When re-validated after parent arrives, full validation runs.

phase1_structural_analysis.findings: The DelayUntilParent return happens at line 2134, before KZG verification at 2185-2190. No expensive ops during queue insertion.

phase2_semantic_analysis.findings: Queue insertion is cheap (no KZG). Re-validation on parent arrival triggers KZG. Per-parent limits needed to bound re-validation cost.
phase2_semantic_analysis.attack_vectors: If attacker sends many sidecars for same parent, all trigger KZG when parent arrives. Need per-parent limits.

phase3_classification.reasoning: Queue insertion is cheap, but re-validation amplification needs per-parent sidecar limits.
phase3_classification.recommended_action: Verify per-parent sidecar limits (at most NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS per block).

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-003: Does DataColumnSidecarsByRange return ResourceUnavailable(3) for out-of-range requests without leaking storage state information?
audit_items.code_excerpt_summary: The handler clamps start_slot to FULU_FORK_EPOCH start (line 1317-1319). No explicit ResourceUnavailable error returned; it just returns whatever is in storage.

phase1_structural_analysis.findings: Line 1316-1319 has TODO and clamps start_slot to fulu_fork_epoch. No explicit out-of-range error response. Storage is queried and results returned.

phase2_semantic_analysis.findings: The handler doesn't return ResourceUnavailable(3) for out-of-range. It adjusts the range and returns whatever storage has. This differs from spec.
phase2_semantic_analysis.attack_vectors: Storage state probing possible by comparing responses for different ranges near boundaries.

phase3_classification.reasoning: The TODO at line 1316 acknowledges incomplete MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS_REQUESTS handling. No explicit ResourceUnavailable error.
phase3_classification.recommended_action: Implement proper ResourceUnavailable(3) response for out-of-range requests per spec.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Is the serve_range boundary calculation consistent and not leaking through response variations?
audit_items.code_excerpt_summary: data_column_serve_range_slot correctly calculates: max(current_epoch - min_epochs_for_data_column_sidecars_requests, fulu_fork_epoch) and converts to slot.

phase1_structural_analysis.findings: Line 774-783 implements correct serve_range calculation with max() and epoch-to-slot conversion.

phase2_semantic_analysis.findings: The serve_range calculation is deterministic based on current_slot and config. Consistent across calls.
phase2_semantic_analysis.attack_vectors: If serve_range is applied inconsistently, response variations could leak storage state.

phase3_classification.reasoning: The serve_range calculation is correct and deterministic. Used consistently in sync logic.
phase3_classification.recommended_action: Ensure serve_range is applied in P2P handlers for out-of-range rejection.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Are timing side channels eliminated for out-of-range DataColumnSidecarsByRange requests?
audit_items.code_excerpt_summary: The handler spawns an async task that queries storage. Timing varies based on storage state, not on range validity.

phase1_structural_analysis.findings: Range check (line 1316-1319) happens before storage query (line 1340). Storage query timing could vary.

phase2_semantic_analysis.findings: No constant-time handling for out-of-range requests. Storage operations timing varies based on data presence.
phase2_semantic_analysis.attack_vectors: Timing analysis could reveal storage state differences for near-boundary requests.

phase3_classification.reasoning: Timing side channels are difficult to exploit in practice over network. Low severity.
phase3_classification.recommended_action: Consider early return with constant-time error for clearly out-of-range requests.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Does the node's sync state remain hidden from out-of-range request probing?
audit_items.code_excerpt_summary: The handler returns available sidecars regardless of sync state. No explicit sync state protection.

phase1_structural_analysis.findings: No sync state checks in the handler. Returns whatever storage has within the adjusted range.

phase2_semantic_analysis.findings: Response content reveals storage state which correlates with sync progress. No explicit sync state hiding.
phase2_semantic_analysis.attack_vectors: Attackers can probe storage contents to fingerprint sync state, but this is low severity.

phase3_classification.reasoning: Some sync state leakage is inevitable when serving data. Not a critical vulnerability.
phase3_classification.recommended_action: None required. Low severity information disclosure.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-001: Does the gossip validation pipeline return IGNORE (not REJECT) for sidecars with slots at or before the finalized epoch's start slot?
audit_items.code_excerpt_summary: Lines 2080-2083: If block_header.slot <= finalized_slot(), returns DataColumnSidecarAction::Ignore(false). This is IGNORE, not REJECT.

phase1_structural_analysis.findings: Line 2081-2083 returns Ignore(false) for slots at or before finalized_slot. Back sync origin bypasses this check.

phase2_semantic_analysis.findings: Correctly uses IGNORE for finalized-slot sidecars. The condition is slot <= finalized_slot() which matches spec.
phase2_semantic_analysis.attack_vectors: Correct IGNORE behavior prevents penalizing peers sending stale sidecars during reorgs.

phase3_classification.reasoning: The implementation correctly returns IGNORE for finalized-slot sidecars.
phase3_classification.recommended_action: None required. Implementation is correct.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Is compute_start_slot_at_epoch correctly implemented and consistent across the gossip validation pipeline?
audit_items.code_excerpt_summary: compute_start_slot_at_epoch is a standard helper function: epoch * SLOTS_PER_EPOCH. Used consistently throughout codebase.

phase1_structural_analysis.findings: compute_start_slot_at_epoch is used at line 2080 via self.finalized_slot() which internally uses compute_start_slot_at_epoch.

phase2_semantic_analysis.findings: Standard spec function. Rust type system prevents overflow via Slot type.
phase2_semantic_analysis.attack_vectors: No overflow vulnerabilities due to type bounds.

phase3_classification.reasoning: Standard spec function implemented correctly.
phase3_classification.recommended_action: None required.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Does the distinction between IGNORE and REJECT correctly affect peer scoring for finalized-slot sidecars?
audit_items.code_excerpt_summary: Returns Ignore action. Peer scoring based on action type is handled in P2P layer.

phase1_structural_analysis.findings: Validation returns DataColumnSidecarAction::Ignore. P2P layer translates this to MessageAcceptance::Ignore (no penalty).

phase2_semantic_analysis.findings: The Ignore action should map to no peer penalty. REJECT errors (ensure! failures) map to penalties.
phase2_semantic_analysis.attack_vectors: Incorrect action-to-penalty mapping could penalize honest peers during reorgs.

phase3_classification.reasoning: The validation layer correctly distinguishes IGNORE from REJECT. P2P layer mapping needs verification.
phase3_classification.recommended_action: Verify P2P layer correctly maps Ignore action to no peer penalty.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-001: Does the gossip validation pipeline REJECT (not IGNORE) sidecars whose parent block has FAILED validation?
audit_items.code_excerpt_summary: Lines 2118-2129 check rejected_block_roots and REJECT if parent is in the set. Lines 2139-2146 check parent_payload_status.is_invalid() and REJECT.

phase1_structural_analysis.findings: Line 2122-2129: ensure! rejects if parent in rejected_block_roots. Line 2141-2146: ensure! rejects if parent_payload_status.is_invalid().

phase2_semantic_analysis.findings: Correctly uses REJECT (ensure!) for known-invalid parent. Both rejected_block_roots and payload_status checks are present.
phase2_semantic_analysis.attack_vectors: Correct REJECT behavior prevents resource waste from queuing sidecars for invalid parents.

phase3_classification.reasoning: The implementation correctly REJECTs sidecars with known-invalid parents through two checks.
phase3_classification.recommended_action: None required. Implementation is correct.

audit_items.title: Critical Boundary Check: Is the invalid-parent block status correctly tracked and queryable by the gossip validation pipeline?
audit_items.code_excerpt_summary: rejected_block_roots is a set in fork_choice_store that tracks invalid block roots. Queried at line 2123-2125.

phase1_structural_analysis.findings: rejected_block_roots is checked via contains(). The set is maintained by the fork choice store when blocks fail validation.

phase2_semantic_analysis.findings: The rejected_block_roots set provides efficient O(1) lookup. Retention policy needs verification.
phase2_semantic_analysis.attack_vectors: If rejected roots are evicted too quickly, sidecars for invalid parents could be queued instead of rejected.

phase3_classification.reasoning: rejected_block_roots lookup is correct. Retention policy needs verification to ensure coverage.
phase3_classification.recommended_action: Verify rejected_block_roots retention covers gossip window duration.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Does the gossip validation correctly distinguish between 'parent not seen' (IGNORE) vs 'parent known-invalid' (REJECT)?
audit_items.code_excerpt_summary: Order: 1) Check rejected_block_roots (REJECT), 2) Check parent_info() presence (IGNORE if None), 3) Check payload_status (REJECT if invalid).

phase1_structural_analysis.findings: Lines 2122-2129 reject if in rejected_block_roots, lines 2131-2137 ignore if parent not found, lines 2141-2146 reject if payload invalid.

phase2_semantic_analysis.findings: Correct distinction: rejected_block_roots checked first (REJECT), then parent presence (IGNORE if not found), then payload status (REJECT if invalid).
phase2_semantic_analysis.attack_vectors: Correct state machine prevents confusion between IGNORE and REJECT.

phase3_classification.reasoning: The implementation correctly distinguishes all three parent states with appropriate actions.
phase3_classification.recommended_action: None required. State machine is correct.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Are sidecars awaiting unknown parents correctly transitioned to REJECT when the parent is later validated as invalid?
audit_items.code_excerpt_summary: When a block is marked invalid, pending sidecars with that parent should be removed from the queue and rejected.

phase1_structural_analysis.findings: Need to verify mutator handles pending sidecar cleanup when parent block validation fails.

phase2_semantic_analysis.findings: If pending sidecars aren't removed when parent is marked invalid, they waste queue space and may be re-validated incorrectly.
phase2_semantic_analysis.attack_vectors: Resource waste if invalid-parent sidecars remain queued indefinitely.

phase3_classification.reasoning: Pending sidecar cleanup on parent invalidation needs verification in mutator.
phase3_classification.recommended_action: Verify pending sidecars are removed when their parent block is marked invalid.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-011: Does the gossip validation pipeline REJECT sidecars where proposer_index does not match the deterministic proposer lookahead (EIP-7917)?
audit_items.code_excerpt_summary: Lines 2199-2207: Computes expected proposer via get_beacon_proposer_index() and ensure! rejects on mismatch.

phase1_structural_analysis.findings: Line 2199 computes expected proposer, lines 2201-2207 use ensure! to reject mismatched proposer_index.

phase2_semantic_analysis.findings: Correctly REJECTs proposer_index mismatch. The computation uses state at the block's slot for shuffling.
phase2_semantic_analysis.attack_vectors: Attackers with valid validator keys cannot claim slots they aren't assigned.

phase3_classification.reasoning: Proposer validation correctly rejects mismatched proposer_index using deterministic computation.
phase3_classification.recommended_action: None required. Implementation is correct.

audit_items.title: Critical Boundary Check: Is the deterministic proposer lookahead (EIP-7917) correctly computed and not using stale shuffling data?
audit_items.code_excerpt_summary: get_beacon_proposer_index uses the state provided to validation. State is retrieved via state_fn() for the appropriate slot.

phase1_structural_analysis.findings: Proposer computation uses state from state_fn() which should be appropriate for block_header.slot.

phase2_semantic_analysis.findings: State retrieval logic (state_cache.existing_state_at_slot) should provide correct state for shuffling. Caching must be invalidated appropriately.
phase2_semantic_analysis.attack_vectors: Stale state could produce wrong proposer assignment. State cache invalidation is critical.

phase3_classification.reasoning: Correct state retrieval depends on state_cache implementation. Cache invalidation needs verification.
phase3_classification.recommended_action: Verify state_cache provides correct non-stale state for proposer computation.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Is proposer signature verification correctly coupled with proposer_index validation?
audit_items.code_excerpt_summary: Signature verification at 2106-2116 uses block_header.proposer_index for pubkey lookup. This is BEFORE proposer_index validation at 2199.

phase1_structural_analysis.findings: Signature verification uses the claimed proposer_index to get pubkey (line 2114). Proposer_index validation comes after (line 2199).

phase2_semantic_analysis.findings: The order is: signature verification with claimed proposer -> then validate proposer is correct. This verifies the claimed proposer signed it, then verifies they should have been the proposer.
phase2_semantic_analysis.attack_vectors: An attacker signing with wrong validator key fails signature check. Signing with right key but wrong slot fails proposer check.

phase3_classification.reasoning: Two-phase validation: 1) signature matches claimed proposer, 2) claimed proposer is correct for slot. Both must pass.
phase3_classification.recommended_action: None required. Two-phase validation is secure.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Does the validation correctly handle the case when shuffling is NOT yet available for the sidecar's slot?
audit_items.code_excerpt_summary: If state_fn() returns None, the function returns DataColumnSidecarAction::DelayUntilState. Sidecar is queued, not rejected.

phase1_structural_analysis.findings: Lines 2096-2104: Returns DelayUntilState when state unavailable. This is safe IGNORE behavior until state is ready.

phase2_semantic_analysis.findings: Correctly delays validation when shuffling/state unavailable. Does NOT accept without proposer verification.
phase2_semantic_analysis.attack_vectors: Safe behavior - sidecar queued until state available, never accepted without full validation.

phase3_classification.reasoning: DelayUntilState is safe handling - queues sidecar for later full validation including proposer check.
phase3_classification.recommended_action: None required. Safe handling of unavailable state.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-006: Is BlobSidecarsByRoot deprecated protocol serve_range correctly bounded to [max(current_epoch - MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOB_SIDECARS_REQUESTS, DENEB_FORK_EPOCH), FULU_FORK_EPOCH)?
audit_items.code_excerpt_summary: TODO at line 1395 indicates MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOB_SIDECARS_REQUESTS not implemented. No serve_range bounds checking.

phase1_structural_analysis.findings: Line 1395 has TODO for MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOB_SIDECARS_REQUESTS. No epoch-based serve_range validation in handler.

phase2_semantic_analysis.findings: Missing serve_range bounds. The handler serves all requested blobs without epoch validation.
phase2_semantic_analysis.attack_vectors: Requests for out-of-range blobs (too old or post-Fulu) not properly rejected.

phase3_classification.reasoning: TODO confirms missing implementation. serve_range bounds not enforced.
phase3_classification.recommended_action: Implement epoch-based serve_range validation per spec.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Does the serve_range lower bound correctly handle the max() between retention window and DENEB_FORK_EPOCH?
audit_items.code_excerpt_summary: blob_serve_range_slot function calculates correct lower bound with max(). Similar to data_column_serve_range_slot.

phase1_structural_analysis.findings: blob_serve_range_slot (similar to data_column_serve_range_slot) implements max() correctly. But not applied in P2P handler.

phase2_semantic_analysis.findings: Helper function exists but not used in BlobSidecarsByRoot handler.
phase2_semantic_analysis.attack_vectors: Lower bound not enforced allows serving blobs older than retention window.

phase3_classification.reasoning: Helper exists but not used in handler. Missing serve_range enforcement.
phase3_classification.recommended_action: Use blob_serve_range_slot in BlobSidecarsByRoot handler.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Is the FULU_FORK_EPOCH upper bound (exclusive) correctly enforced for BlobSidecarsByRoot requests?
audit_items.code_excerpt_summary: No FULU_FORK_EPOCH upper bound check in handler. All requested blobs served regardless of epoch.

phase1_structural_analysis.findings: No epoch comparison against FULU_FORK_EPOCH in the handler. Post-Fulu blobs could be served.

phase2_semantic_analysis.findings: Missing upper bound check. Post-Fulu, this protocol should be fully deprecated.
phase2_semantic_analysis.attack_vectors: Post-Fulu blobs served through deprecated protocol violates deprecation.

phase3_classification.reasoning: No FULU_FORK_EPOCH check. Deprecated protocol incorrectly serves post-Fulu data.
phase3_classification.recommended_action: Add FULU_FORK_EPOCH upper bound check to reject post-Fulu blob requests.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Is the BlobSidecarsByRoot deprecated protocol consistent with BlobSidecarsByRange in serve_range enforcement?
audit_items.code_excerpt_summary: Both BlobSidecarsByRoot and BlobSidecarsByRange handlers have TODOs for MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOB_SIDECARS_REQUESTS.

phase1_structural_analysis.findings: Both handlers have similar TODOs at lines 1395 and in the range handler. Neither enforces serve_range.

phase2_semantic_analysis.findings: Consistent in their incompleteness - both missing serve_range enforcement. At least they're equally (in)complete.
phase2_semantic_analysis.attack_vectors: Both protocols equally lack deprecation enforcement.

phase3_classification.reasoning: Consistently missing serve_range in both deprecated blob protocols.
phase3_classification.recommended_action: Implement consistent serve_range in both BlobSidecarsByRoot and BlobSidecarsByRange.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-006: Are peers protected from scoring penalties when using deprecated BlobSidecarsByRoot protocol during the transition period?
audit_items.code_excerpt_summary: Handler processes requests without peer penalties. No explicit transition period handling but no penalties applied.

phase1_structural_analysis.findings: The handler doesn't apply peer penalties for deprecated protocol use. It just processes requests normally.

phase2_semantic_analysis.findings: No explicit transition period handling, but also no penalties applied. De facto graceful degradation.
phase2_semantic_analysis.attack_vectors: No risk of incorrect peer penalization since no penalties are applied.

phase3_classification.reasoning: No peer penalties for deprecated protocol use. Graceful degradation by default.
phase3_classification.recommended_action: None required for peer scoring. Serve_range enforcement still needed.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Does the beacon-node correctly identify deprecated protocol requests as legitimate during transition?
audit_items.code_excerpt_summary: All BlobSidecarsByRoot requests handled identically. No classification as deprecated/malicious.

phase1_structural_analysis.findings: No request classification logic. All requests treated as legitimate.

phase2_semantic_analysis.findings: No differentiation between deprecated and current protocol usage. All requests processed.
phase2_semantic_analysis.attack_vectors: No incorrect classification risk since all requests treated same.

phase3_classification.reasoning: No request classification means no misclassification risk.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Is the BlobSidecarsByRoot deprecated protocol peer scoring consistent with BlobSidecarsByRange?
audit_items.code_excerpt_summary: Both handlers process requests without peer scoring penalties. Consistent behavior.

phase1_structural_analysis.findings: Both deprecated blob protocol handlers have similar structure without peer penalties.

phase2_semantic_analysis.findings: Consistent peer scoring (none) between both deprecated protocols.
phase2_semantic_analysis.attack_vectors: No inconsistent penalty risk.

phase3_classification.reasoning: Consistent handling between both deprecated blob protocols.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Does graceful degradation prevent network fragmentation during transition?
audit_items.code_excerpt_summary: No peer disconnection or penalties for deprecated protocol use. Nodes remain connected.

phase1_structural_analysis.findings: Handler doesn't disconnect peers or apply penalties. Network remains connected.

phase2_semantic_analysis.findings: Graceful degradation achieved - no fragmentation risk from deprecated protocol handling.
phase2_semantic_analysis.attack_vectors: No network fragmentation from transition.

phase3_classification.reasoning: No peer penalties or disconnections prevents network fragmentation.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-003: Is DataColumnSidecarsByRange response limited to count * NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS sidecars?
audit_items.code_excerpt_summary: Handler uses max_request_data_column_sidecars limit (line 1331-1335) passed to storage query. count-based limit is implicit via slot range.

phase1_structural_analysis.findings: max_request_data_column_sidecars is used at line 1343. The count is limited by MAX_FOR_DOS_PREVENTION (line 1320). Combined limits apply.

phase2_semantic_analysis.findings: Two limits: 1) MAX_FOR_DOS_PREVENTION on count (64), 2) max_request_data_column_sidecars from config. Response size bounded.
phase2_semantic_analysis.attack_vectors: Response size is bounded. count * NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS implicit through range and column filtering.

phase3_classification.reasoning: Response bounded by max_request_data_column_sidecars and count limits. Implicit count * NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS via range.
phase3_classification.recommended_action: Verify max_request_data_column_sidecars >= count * NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS for typical requests.
